data.content_ref: inline:§11.3 flags are sustained because the two critics were tested on the same artifact (0c61961a8085 / SRC_005) and both were found to have failed, which implies either (a) the critics share a common failure mode or (b) the test case itself is degenerate. Under the mechanist stance: if two independently-designed critics both produce the same verdict-class (failure) on the same input, the most economical causal explanation is a shared structural assumption (e.g., both use threshold-based frontier detection with the same floor value) rather than a shared reasoning error. The flag persists because the audit procedure treats repeated failure as evidence of critic deficiency when it is actually evidence of a test-design deficiency: a single non-discriminating test case was used to adjudicate two distinct critics.
